question:
An engineer must implement Strict Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding mode for IPv4 packets on the Etnerret1/1 interface on the Cisco Nexus 9500 Series Switch.
Which configuration achieves this goal?
options: interface Ethernet1/1 ip address 172.16.10.1/24 ip verify unicast source reachable-via rx
interface Ethernet1/1 ip address 172.16.10.1/24 ip verify unicast source any
interface Ethernet1/1 ip address 172.16.10.1/24 ip verify unicast source reachable-via any
interface Ethernet1/1 ip address 172.16.10.1/24 ip verify unicast source rx
theory: Just as on other Nexus platforms, the command ip verify unicast source reachable-via rx applied under an interface enables strict Unicast RPF, requiring that an incoming packet's source address be reachable specifically through the receiving interface (a symmetric-routing check), which blocks spoofed-source traffic. The 'reachable-via any' or bare 'any' variants instead configure loose mode, which only checks that the source exists anywhere in the routing table. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 18 - Nexus First-Hop Security / uRPF)
